name: Deep sail snail

baseline.name: Deep sail snail
baseline.look: Large pale marine snail with a ridged buoyant shell and trailing sensory fronds.
baseline.ecology: Grazes floating fungal mats; empty shells become instruments.
baseline.limit: Living shells are fragile; removing them kills the animal.
baseline.encounter: Harvest only shed mineral fragments and naturally empty shells.
baseline.scale_note: Adult representative staging envelope; individuals vary by up to 10%. Not shown at common scale on the art plate.

daily: A deep sail snail grazes floating fungal mats with slow rhythmic mouth movements. Buoyancy comes from its ridged shell; sensory fronds track nearby water and surfaces.
cycle: Small juveniles shelter beneath healthy mats. Live shell damage reduces buoyancy and exposes tissue. Empty shells enter the material economy only after natural death.
signs: Fresh curved grazing edges show an occupied mat. A drifting shell is not necessarily empty: tenders check for retracted tissue without tearing it free.
escalation: Graze -> retract fronds -> withdraw -> drift with current. It does not consent to being handled simply because it cannot flee quickly.
community: Lumen Tide craftspeople mark the provenance of naturally empty shells and gather shed mineral fragments. Fast tourist demand can make a truthful supply chain valuable.
scene: A beautiful instrument comes with an impossible harvest date. Namu must question a respected maker without condemning the whole craft tradition.
motion: Shell remains rigid; foot and fronds move slowly beneath it. Do not turn a living shell into a detachable hat.
sounds: Soft grazing rasp and tiny shell contacts. Instrument tones belong to empty shells used by makers, not animal speech.
rule: Living shells cannot be removed without killing the animal. No instant regrowth or endless shell farming.
canon_status: Additive ecology and production guidance; proposed scene remains unadopted.
